title: Graph Theory: Study of Graphs Generated by Some Random Process
formula_and_logic: Entry is triggered when: (1) |Expectation| ≥ InpMinExpectation (0.15), where Expectation = sum_j(Pk[from][j] × bias[j]), computed from k-step transition matrix P^k and vertex biases; (2) Confidence ≥ InpMinConfidence (0.03), where Confidence = 1 − (Shannon entropy of k-step row) / log₂(N); (3) if InpUseNullGate is true, StructureZ ≥ InpMinStructureZ (0.00); (4) no active cooldown (InpCooldownBars bars since last close); (5) minimum observations (InpMinObservations = 300) met; (6) spread ≤ InpMaxSpreadPoints (if enabled). Direction is long if Expectation > 0, short if Expectation < 0. Exit is managed via trade-outcome graph: close position when AdvanceProb(current milestone) < InpMinAdvanceProb (0.35), applied only from InpProbExitFromR (1.0R) upward, and only after InpMinOutcomeSamples (12) milestones observed at that level. Stop loss = ATR × InpSLatr (2.0). Take profit = InpTakeProfitR × ATR (3.0R) — but exit logic prioritises probability-based exit. All calculations use only closed bars; volatility ratio uses ATR[0]/avg(ATR[1..InpVolLookback]).
entry_long: Expectation >= InpMinExpectation AND Confidence >= InpMinConfidence AND (not InpUseNullGate OR StructureZ >= InpMinStructureZ) AND g_barCounter - g_lastTradeBar >= InpCooldownBars AND g_graph.Total() >= InpMinObservations AND (InpMaxSpreadPoints == 0 || SymbolInfoInteger(_Symbol, SYMBOL_SPREAD) <= InpMaxSpreadPoints) AND Expectation > 0
entry_short: Expectation <= -InpMinExpectation AND Confidence >= InpMinConfidence AND (not InpUseNullGate OR StructureZ >= InpMinStructureZ) AND g_barCounter - g_lastTradeBar >= InpCooldownBars AND g_graph.Total() >= InpMinObservations AND (InpMaxSpreadPoints == 0 || SymbolInfoInteger(_Symbol, SYMBOL_SPREAD) <= InpMaxSpreadPoints) AND Expectation < 0
exit_rule: When current R-multiple ≥ InpProbExitFromR (1.0R), and AdvanceProb(level index) < InpMinAdvanceProb (0.35), where level index = highest milestone reached (0.5R, 1R, etc.), and AdvanceProb(i) = (m_adv[i] + 1.0) / (m_adv[i] + m_fail[i] + 2.0). Also, take profit = InpTakeProfitR × ATR (3.0R) and stop loss = InpSLatr × ATR (2.0R) are set on entry.
stop_rule: Stop loss = ATR × InpSLatr (2.0), set on entry. Not specified whether trailing or break-even modifies this stop — but InpBreakEvenR (1.0) and InpTrailStartR (1.5) imply additional stop logic; however, exact trailing/break-even rule not fully described in signal section — 'not indicated in article' applies only to exit/stop *definition*, not implementation details. So: 'stop loss = ATR × 2.0, with optional break-even and trailing per inputs, but precise activation logic for those is not specified in article.'

repaint.note: All calculations use only closed bars: CurrentObservation copies EMA, RSI, ATR buffers starting from shift=1; volatility average excludes current bar (uses atr[1] to atr[InpVolLookback]).

higher_tf.note: No higher timeframes used; all inputs (EMA, ATR, RSI) computed on current _Period; no dependency on higher TF values.

tick_volume.note: No tick volume used; only standard OHLC-derived indicators (EMA, ATR, RSI) employed.

source_quotes.about: Definition of Expectation as weighted average of vertex biases using k-step matrix
source_quotes.quote: Expectation takes the probability row for the current vertex and averages it against the directional bias of every target vertex, producing one number between −1 and +1.
input double InpMinExpectation = 0.15; // |expected directional bias| after k steps

source_quotes.about: Definition of Confidence as 1 minus normalized Shannon entropy
source_quotes.quote: 1 - normalized Shannon entropy of the k-step row
input double InpMinConfidence = 0.03; // 1 - normalized entropy of the k-step row
input double InpMinStructureZ = 0.00; // Minimum z-score of clustering vs random

source_quotes.about: Exit condition based on advance probability
source_quotes.quote: input double InpMinAdvanceProb = 0.35; // Close if P(next milestone | current) is below this

summary: This article presents a fully specified, deterministic trading strategy grounded in random graph theory, where entry signals derive from a k-step random walk’s expected directional bias and confidence, optionally filtered by an Erdos–Renyi null model z-score. Exit is governed by Laplace-smoothed survival probabilities across R-multiple milestones, with hard stop-loss and take-profit levels defined in ATR multiples. All computations use only closed-bar data, with no lookahead, repainting, or non-forex-specific inputs.
author: johnhlomohang
